title: Model thousandths: 1 whole = 10 tenths = 100 hundredths = 1000 thousandths

lesson.title: Meet the Thousandths!

steps.say: You already know how to break one whole into ten tenths, and how to split it even further into one hundred tiny hundredths. Today we take one more little step and cut those hundredths into even smaller pieces called thousandths.

Here is the trick. Take just one of those little hundredth squares and slice it into ten skinny strips. Each strip is one thousandth. Since there are one hundred little squares, and each one gives ten strips, one hundred times ten is one thousand. So one whole holds one thousand thousandths.

visual.caption: Slice this 1 shaded hundredth into 10 strips → each strip is 1 thousandth

steps.say: Let's line up the whole family with base ten blocks. Imagine the big flat square is one whole. Then a rod is one tenth, a little cube is one hundredth, and if we could snip that little cube into ten slivers, each sliver would be one thousandth. Ten tenths, one hundred hundredths, one thousand thousandths — they all make the very same one whole.

visual.caption: 1 flat = 1 whole, 1 rod = 1 tenth, 1 cube = 1 hundredth

steps.say: Now a real example. A loonie is one dollar, and one whole dollar is one hundred pennies, so a penny is one hundredth of a dollar. Now think about a milk carton at the store in Vancouver that holds one litre. One litre is one thousand millilitres, so one millilitre is one thousandth of a litre. If you shade three of the little hundredth squares, that is three hundredths, and three hundredths is the same as thirty thousandths, because each hundredth is worth ten thousandths.

Here is a mix-up lots of kids make. Someone sees one thousandth and thinks it must be bigger than one hundredth, because one thousand is a bigger number than one hundred. But it is the other way around. The more pieces you cut the whole into, the smaller each piece gets. Cutting a pizza into one thousand slices gives way tinier slices than cutting it into one hundred. So one thousandth is the smallest of the three.

visual.caption: 0.01 and 0.001 are both tiny — 0.001 is smaller

steps.say: So remember, the whole never changes size. We just keep slicing it into more and more, smaller and smaller, equal pieces.

visual.caption: Always one whole — just chopped up finer

lesson.answer: One whole stays one whole: 10 tenths, 100 hundredths, or 1000 thousandths — more pieces means smaller pieces.

practice.question: Draw a big square and split it into 100 little squares, so the whole square is one litre of maple syrup. Shade in 7 of the little squares. How many hundredths of a litre did you shade, and how many thousandths of a litre is that? (Hint: each little square can be cut into 10 skinny strips.)
practice.answer: 7 hundredths of a litre, which is the same as 70 thousandths of a litre (7 times 10 equals 70), and that is 70 millilitres.
